title: Introduce telemetry conciliator, compact token-sig index, and route-aware alert calibrator
author: Maya Kapoor
description:
Motivation:
Production alert noise and unexplained token-cost regressions have two recurring causes: (1) divergence between short-window high-cardinality rollups and long-window aggregated metrics, and (2) lack of a compact, privacy-preserving way to attribute token-level cost spikes to invocation traces. This PR introduces the 'telemetry conciliator' — a reconciliation layer that harmonizes short/long rollups and provides a compact token-signature index to speed cross-reference between traces, logs, and cost rollups.

What this PR changes (overview):
- telemetry conciliator service (in-process library + thin API): aligns incremental rollups between 1m/5m/1h windows, emits reconciliation markers and suppressed-noise hints for downstream alerting.
- token-sig-index: a compact, salted hash signature per token-sequence prefix that is stored in a KV index (sharded by tenant). The index stores: token-sig, downsampled-cost, canonical-span-id, and time-bucket pointers. The signatures are irreversible and keyed by a per-tenant salt to avoid cross-tenant linkage.
- route-aware alert calibrator: calibration layer that consumes reconciliation markers + route seasonality profiles and adjusts alert thresholds (quiet windows, hysteresis, and dynamic dampening) to reduce churn on long-tail routes. Uses a lightweight Gaussian-process-based baseline fitter for seasonal drift.
- dashboards & docs: new conciliator overview dashboard (latency vs reconciliation offset), token-sig heatmap, and an alert-calibration debug view. Added docs for operators on how to interpret reconciliation markers and how to opt-in per-tenant.

Design notes and privacy:
- token signatures are salted SHA-256 truncations + Blake2 compression; we store only 64-bit digest. The code explicitly rejects capture of raw token text in any trace/span. Salt is tenant-specific and managed through the existing KMS pipeline.
- Conciliation is deterministic and idempotent: we compute reconciliation deltas at emit-time and attach reconciliation vector metadata to existing metric series (no separate metric namespace required).

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default state is opt-out for Private installations; Hosted customers are rolled out via feature-flag. Reconciler emits non-breaking span tags and reconciliation-* metrics; consumers that don't consume them see no behavioral change. Alert calibrator is initially in 'suggest' mode (does not alter thresholds) for two weeks in staging, then promoted to active calibrator with operator approval.
- Fallback: if the token-sig-index is unavailable for a tenant, conciliator emits a NULL-sig marker and alert-calibrator uses coarse-grain route baselines only.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests cover index read/write, salt rotation, reconciliation vector generation and calibrator damping behaviors.
- E2E smoke harness runs reconciler on a replayed week of synthetic invocations and verifies alert reduction without increasing missed-SLOs (benchmarks included).

Risk & mitigations:
- Performance: KV-backed index introduced a small write cost; conciliator batches signature writes with adaptive backoff and monitors local queue length. Benchmarks show 1.8% P50 token-path latency increase at 99th percentile traffic; autoscaler and batching thresholds tuned to keep this <3%.
- Privacy: strong requirement (see above). Security reviewed and signed off by security team (Aria).

Related: ENG-9876 (telemetry reconciler epic), ENG-12830 (alerting calibration work), SUP-3412 (customer report that triggered investigation).

review_comments: Diego Silva: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: add a short-circuit path when index latency > 200ms and document how salt rotation affects historical attribution.

Maya Kapoor (author): Added short-circuit path + metrics emitted when index latency exceeds threshold. Clarified salt-rotation behavior in docs (we only re-index new signatures; old digests remain valid but are marked legacy).
Aria Chen: Security note: ensure salt is never logged; confirm KMS envelope key rotation doesn't leak mapping. Please add a test that simulates key rotation.
Maya Kapoor (author): Added key-rotation unit test and explicit logging guard. Security sign-off provided.
Liam O'Neill: Alert calibrator looks promising — request to add a 'dry-run' UI flag for playbook operators. Also, CI flaky test in e2e harness flagged; I re-ran the job.
Maya Kapoor (author): Added dry-run operator flag and fixed e2e harness seed; CI re-run now green.
Repo Maintainer: approved and merged via squash after CI passed.
release_notes: Introduced telemetry conciliator, token-sig compact index, and route-aware alert calibrator. Reduces alert churn on long-tail routes and enables faster, privacy-preserving attribution of token-level cost spikes. Opt-in for Private installs; Hosted rollout behind feature flag.
privacy_notes: Token signatures are stored as salted 64-bit digests; raw token text is never persisted. Salt is tenant-scoped and managed via KMS. Security reviewed and approved.
notes_for_oncall: If you see reconciliation-offset > 5m or index-write-latency > 500ms alerts, the conciliator will fallback to coarse baselines; check conciliator queue length metric and KV backend availability. Dry-run mode for calibrator leaves thresholds unchanged (check alert-calibrator.mode).
